learningObjective: Reason about which operations can be fused as a GEMM epilogue and what the HBM-traffic benefit is.

canonicalClaims.claim: Bias-add and elementwise activation fuse naturally as GEMM epilogues on tensor-core GPUs, saving one HBM roundtrip per intermediate; RMSNorm/LayerNorm require a per-row reduction that conflicts with typical GEMM tile decomposition and is usually kept as a separate kernel or handled by a specialized row-reduce epilogue.
conditions: GEMM library (CUTLASS, cuBLASLt) supports elementwise epilogue.
GEMM tile does not span full row for norm fusion.
nonImplications: Does not imply RMSNorm is never fused; specialized full-row-tile GEMMs can fuse it.
Does not imply epilogue fusion always reduces total compute; it reduces HBM traffic.

misconceptions.claim: RMSNorm is a pure elementwise op that fuses like GELU.
misconceptions.whyWrong: RMSNorm needs the per-row RMS statistic; it is not elementwise.
Tensor-core outputs are consumed by epilogue instructions in registers/SMEM without a throughput penalty.

misconceptions.claim: All post-GEMM ops can be fused as epilogue.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Ops that need cross-tile reductions or global state (softmax, norms) require special handling.

implementationFacts: CUTLASS's epilogue module supports bias, activation, and elementwise scale in a single kernel launch.
TensorRT-LLM defines fused-kernel plugins for common LLM epilogues.
performanceScenarios: Bias/activation epilogue is essentially free on tensor-core-driven GEMMs.
Row-reduce epilogues (LayerNorm/RMSNorm) are supported in specialized libraries but with tile-shape constraints.
